question: A Year 8 student is solving a problem involving recognise the connection between exponent form and expanded form with the exponent laws of product of powers rule quotient of powers rule and power of a power rule. Which option is mathematically valid?
audio_prompt: A Year 8 student is solving a problem involving recognise the connection between exponent form and expanded form with the exponent laws of product of powers rule quotient of powers rule and power of a power rule. Which option is mathematically valid?

answers.text: recognising the connection between exponent form and expanded form with the exponent laws of product of powers rule, quotient of powers rule, and power of a power rule; for example, 2^3\times2^2 can be represented as (2\times2\times2)\times(2\times2)=2^5 and connecting the result to the addition of exponents
Exact and approximate values are treated as interchangeable
